public_rationale: For January–March 2026, Microsoft's annualized AI revenue and Amazon's total AWS sales do not establish OpenAI and Anthropic's share of realized AI revenue across Google, Microsoft and Amazon. [e1, e2] Anthropic's October 26 filing supports the annual-loss component for Anthropic: its 2025 net loss was $42 billion, including $34.3 billion in fair-value changes. This is not a cash-burn measure. [e4] The February 27 announcement establishes Amazon's planned, partly conditional investment in OpenAI, but does not show that OpenAI needed new financing to pay current bills. [e3] Anthropic's warning about future profitability does not establish that it lacked a credible route to profitability in January–March 2026. [e4]
limitations: No matching customer-specific and total realized AI revenue figures establish the combined or company-level shares for January–March 2026.
The packet does not establish OpenAI's annual losses or reconcile both labs' operating receipts, available cash and payment obligations.
The investment announcement and Anthropic's loss disclosure do not settle continuing financing necessity or either lab's profitability prospects. [e3, e4]

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Most hyperscaler AI revenue comes from OpenAI and Anthropic, which lose billions, have no path to profitability, and pay only because they are funded.

statement.excerpt: As I’ve explained, most AI revenues out of Google, Microsoft and Amazon come from two companies that lose billions of dollars a year, have no path to profitability, and are only able to keep paying these companies because the companies (and investors) keep feeding them money.
statement.document_title: Am I Meant To Be Impressed?

from_speaker: most AI revenues out of Google, Microsoft and Amazon
two companies that lose billions of dollars a year
only able to keep paying these companies because the companies (and investors) keep feeding them money
our_interpretation: The two companies are OpenAI and Anthropic.
Most means more than 50% of realized AI revenue attributable to these two customers. The main reading combines the three hyperscalers; company-level shares should also be reported.

Use January–March 2026, the latest completed reporting quarter before the post, for the ongoing revenue and financing assertions. Annual losses require separate annual records and cannot be established by annualizing one quarter.
Read no path to profitability as no economically credible route under the business economics then prevailing, rather than a claim that profitability is impossible forever.
Treat the revenue concentration assertion as an estimate inferred from the surrounding discussion of reported financial figures. No GAAP or other formal accounting basis is specified.
Funding dependence requires evidence of a cash shortfall after operating receipts and available cash, rather than merely evidence that fundraising occurred.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable records establish that the two labs generated more than half of the named hyperscalers' realized AI revenue, that both incurred multibillion-dollar annual losses, and that their operating economics required continuing outside financing without a credible route to profitability.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish a combined revenue share of 50% or less, or establish that a lab could sustainably meet its obligations without continuing outside financing. A substantiated route to profitability would contradict that component.

evidence.locator: First-page financial highlights, AWS sales bullet
evidence.explanation: AWS sales include services beyond AI and are not broken down here by the two customers. This is not the denominator asserted in the claim.
This establishes an announced funding relationship. The announcement describes staged, partly conditional funding; it does not establish the necessity of financing for current payments.

evidence.locator: Risk factors, page 64; related quarterly results on page 158
evidence.explanation: The filing acknowledges historical losses and uncertainty about future profitability. Its risk warning does not establish that no credible profitability path existed in the target quarter.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Matching January–March 2026 customer revenue and total AI revenue records for all three hyperscalers, annual loss records for both labs, and contemporaneous cash balances, cash flows, payment schedules and substantiated operating forecasts testing financing necessity and credible routes to profitability.
